answer: Each challenge is cryptographically bound to a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse: its commitment fixes the task, while the later, collectively generated and unbiasable value selects or mutates hidden parameters. Before that pulse, an attacker cannot know the valid workload, so precomputation and offline farming lose value; commit-reveal checks also expose equivocation. A sybil swarm gains no haven, bridge, or ledge for cheaply reusing answers.
